news.headline: Salvadoran Immigrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia Voluntarily Departs U.S. for Spain
news.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national, has agreed to leave the United States for Spain after a 20-month legal dispute with federal immigration authorities. U.S. officials say the departure is voluntary and ends the prolonged case. The outcome ends a high‑profile immigration controversy that began with his mistaken deportation last year. The case highlights ongoing debates over U.S. immigration enforcement policies.

news.headline: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed due to severe weather
news.summary: A nor'easter moving up the East Coast prompted organizers to delay the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City to Saturday. The decision was made after consultations with city officials and the police department, citing safety concerns for participants and spectators. The postponement affects the parade's 100th anniversary celebration and its iconic balloon segment.

news.headline: U.S. Army Reschedules Lead Azide Detonation at Iowa Ammunition Plant
news.summary: The U.S. Army announced that it will conduct a controlled detonation of more than 60 barrels of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The schedule change follows a federal court order that placed an indefinite pause on the operation and ongoing debate over public health and safety. President Trump has said the final decision will depend on court approval and the incoming Iowa governor. The Army says the timing is set to take advantage of optimal weather conditions.

news.headline: Steelers bench veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers amid coach-player clash
news.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers will not play, naming Mason Rudolph as the starter for the upcoming game. Coach Mike McCarthy cited disagreements over the offense as the reason for the benching. Rodgers responded with a heated interview accusing the coach of unprofessional behavior. The move raises questions about Rodgers' future with the team and the franchise's direction.

news.headline: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan seeks court delay of scheduled execution
news.summary: Former Army major Nidal Hasan filed a federal court motion asking to postpone his Dec. 3 military execution by firing squad. He says the delay is needed to pursue a habeas corpus petition challenging his conviction. The request comes as the Pentagon prepares to carry out the execution, which has drawn public attention. The outcome will affect how military death sentences are administered.

news.headline: Federal court unseals search warrant and documents in Ilhan Omar investigation
news.summary: A federal judge ordered the release of a partially redacted search warrant and related filings concerning the raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington, D.C., home. The documents indicate that prosecutors are examining alleged immigration‑related offenses dating back several decades. The release allows the public to see the scope of the Justice Department's inquiry. The case is being closely watched as it involves a sitting member of Congress.

news.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump's second attempt to limit birthright citizenship
news.summary: A U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper issued a preliminary injunction stopping the Trump administration's latest executive order that sought to create new exceptions to the 14th Amendment's birthright citizenship guarantee. The ruling cites the Constitution's Citizenship Clause and prevents the policy from taking effect. The decision marks the second federal court blockage of the administration's efforts to restrict citizenship for children born in the United States. The case highlights ongoing legal battles over executive authority and immigration policy.

news.headline: ICE arrests Massachusetts lottery winner with prior deportation order
news.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales, a man from El Salvador with a 2014 deportation order, after he won a $1 million Massachusetts state lottery prize. The arrest occurred in East Boston following a brief foot chase. Authorities say the detention is related to his illegal immigration status, not the lottery winnings. The case highlights tensions over immigration enforcement and the treatment of undocumented individuals who win large prizes.

news.headline: Trump administration prepares to raise tariffs on China, EU and other partners
news.summary: The White House is set to announce new import taxes on goods from China, the European Union and about a dozen other economies. The tariffs are presented as a response to what officials describe as excess industrial capacity and market distortion abroad. The move follows a Supreme Court decision that struck down earlier sweeping tariff measures. The proposal comes as the administration seeks to revive its broader trade agenda.

news.headline: Sen. Chris Van Hollen Signals Interest in Challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic Leader
news.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said he is "in listening mode" about a possible bid to become the Senate Democratic majority leader, a role currently held by Chuck Schumer. The discussion follows growing calls within the Democratic caucus for a broader leadership contest rather than a predetermined succession. Van Hollen’s potential challenge reflects internal debates over the party’s direction as Democrats prepare for the next Congress. The outcome could reshape Senate leadership and influence the party’s legislative agenda.

satire.headline: Trump Announces Thanksgiving Turkey Won't Be Pardoned, Will Face Firing Squad
satire.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Donald Trump announced today that this year's Thanksgiving Turkey will not be pardoned and will instead face execution by a firing squad. As part of a timeless American tradition, a Thanksgiving turkey has received a pardon from the US President this week, following an unrelated $100 million bribe it made to one of Trump’s businesses.

satire.headline: Disaster As Detonation Leaves Iowa Completely Covered In Popcorn
satire.summary: DES MOINES, IA — The planned detonation of lead azide in Iowa has turned disastrous as the entire state has become engulfed in popcorn.
